branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Unilateral Vision Loss with Macular Edema and Associated Systemic Vascular Risk Factors

state.case_summary:
A 63-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and multiple strokes presented with vision loss in the right eye. The patient had persistent symptoms for 1.5 years with visual acuity ranging between 20/100 to 20/200.

Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed severe macular changes with associated edema.

- Imaging Studies:    1. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography findings:       - Initial scan showed persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 [79.3] μm over 12 visits       - Sequential scans documented changes in macular edema over the course of treatment           Image Titles and Descriptions:     Figure: 'Reversible Effect on Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) Secondary to Retinal Vein Occlusion After Stopping Niacin Therapy'    - Shows series of OCT scans demonstrating changes in macular edema under different treatment conditions

excluded_candidates: Retinal detachment: less likely due to the presence of macular edema and cystoid macular edema
Diabetic retinopathy: less likely due to the absence of diabetes in the patient's history
Other vascular causes: less likely due to the specific pattern of macular edema and associated risk factors
